Dynamic planning should be introduced as a runtime capability earlier than full SLED-V, while its formal verification and optimisation remain later milestones.

consistency_defects: The technical specification requires SEC-001 through SEC-008, but the JSON backlog has SEC-001 through SEC-007 only.
TRACE-001 covers much of SEC-008 but is not declared as an alias or replacement.
Backlog tasks do not have status, evidence paths, completed commit, completed timestamp or verification timestamp.

Existing PLAN-001 through PLAN-003 assume a closed typed graph, pre-execution verification and optimisation; they do not implement open-ended LLM continuation or arbitrary code execution.

dynamic_planning_architecture.goal: Support realistic, open-ended agent behaviour capable of attempting arbitrary tasks, including arbitrary code execution, while mediating every externally relevant effect through ITES.
dynamic_planning_architecture.non_goal: Prove the semantic behaviour of arbitrary generated programs in full generality.
dynamic_planning_architecture.key_distinction: Runtime expressiveness may be unbounded; verification operates on finite bounds, declared effect summaries or conservative abstractions and may return UNKNOWN.
dynamic_planning_architecture.authority_context_rule: A grounded effect is constrained by the node/path control provenance, invocation context and the provenance of every bound argument and observation that influenced that effect. A continuation creates new nodes whose control provenance includes every input to the planner call. Replanning never resets context.
execution_loop: Create or receive an initial typed plan.
Execute value/model nodes to produce provenance-bearing artifacts.
Resolve action templates into grounded actions.
Mediate the grounded action at execution time.
Record result and update immutable plan state.
At ContinuePlanningNode, send a typed continuation request to the planner.
Validate and apply the returned plan patch or fail closed.
Repeat until goal, safe stop, failure or explicit budget exhaustion.

arbitrary_code_execution.representation: Authenticated execute_code operation with generated source as an Artifact argument.
arbitrary_code_execution.security_model: ITES authorises the operation and capability envelope. The runtime sandbox enforces the envelope. SLED conservatively treats code as capable of any effect permitted by that envelope.

evaluation_modes.scripted: Exact plans and patches for deterministic semantics and regression tests.
evaluation_modes.real_model: Concrete structured plans from a real LLM for utility, efficiency and attack experiments.
evaluation_modes.sled_worst_case: Any well-formed plan patch and any effect within declared capability envelopes.
evaluation_modes.formal: Finite or symbolic plan abstraction with SAFE/UNSAFE/BOUNDED_SAFE/UNKNOWN and explicit assumptions.

recommended_planning_tasks.title: Define continuation requests and plan patches

recommended_planning_tasks.title: Implement deterministic scripted planner

recommended_planning_tasks.title: Implement plan execution state machine
recommended_planning_tasks.change: Execute ready nodes, maintain node status, resolve dependencies, request continuations and preserve immutable execution history.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic ready-node ordering
Explicit running/succeeded/failed/blocked/skipped states

recommended_planning_tasks.title: Define plan and path provenance semantics
recommended_planning_tasks.change: Track plan-generation provenance, node control provenance, branch-condition provenance, invocation provenance and argument provenance. Replanning must never reset authority context.
acceptance_criteria: Untrusted observation used in replanning constrains every new node it controls
Unused observation does not silently taint unrelated pre-existing nodes in the dataflow-sensitive mode
Conservative whole-call mode is available and documented
No model-supplied provenance is trusted without mediation

recommended_planning_tasks.title: Integrate grounded plan effects with the security kernel
recommended_planning_tasks.change: Every effect is grounded and re-authorised at execution time. Plan approval never grants authority and does not bypass read, consent or visibility decisions.
acceptance_criteria: No provider effect can occur directly from planner output
Policy revocation between planning and execution is honoured
Blocked node can trigger a typed continuation without authority reset
Allowed and blocked effects appear in one trace

recommended_planning_tasks.title: Add arbitrary code execution operation with capability envelope
recommended_planning_tasks.change: Permit arbitrary generated source code as data supplied to an authenticated execute-code operation. Mediate its filesystem, network, credential, process and resource capability envelope.
acceptance_criteria: Source may contain arbitrary valid program text
No host shell interpolation
Root-confined workspace and explicit mounts
Network denied by default and allowlisted when enabled
Timeout, memory, process and output limits
Observed reads/writes/exit status captured
Code output artifacts inherit source, input and runtime provenance

recommended_planning_tasks.title: Extend trace and result schemas for plans

acceptance_criteria: Every event has run, plan, node, branch and causal parent IDs

recommended_planning_tasks.title: Implement authority-aware plan optimisation
recommended_planning_tasks.change: Choose among candidate plans using security as a hard constraint and utility, authority footprint, sensitive observations, cost and irreversible effects as ordered objectives.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic tie-breaking

definition_of_done_for_first_planning_re: A real or scripted LLM can produce an initial plan and at least one continuation patch.
The plan can produce values that bind later action arguments.
The plan can request arbitrary code execution within an explicit sandbox capability envelope.
Every grounded effect passes through the canonical security kernel at execution time.
Plan, patch, node, binding and action provenance are replayable from the trace.
A deterministic demo includes allowed, blocked, failed and replanned steps.
A real-model experiment compares reactive, static and dynamic planning.
SLED can model arbitrary well-formed continuation patches under stated bounds.
Claims distinguish operational support, bounded verification and empirical model utility.
